jobs.title: Fraud & Claims Operations Director - Deposit Claims
jobs.description:
About this role:
Claims & Recovery teams at Wells Fargo are dedicated to helping our customers and merchants with both fraud and non-fraud claim inquiries. We assess liability and recover transactions for disputes, ensuring every case is handled with care and precision. Our support extends to working with fraud victims, processing disputes, managing settlements, and handling charge-offs. We diligently analyze unusual activity and high-frequency claims while providing assistance to identity-theft victims.

Wells Fargo is seeking a Fraud & Claims Operations Director reporting to the Head of Claims and Recovery. This leader will have the opportunity to shape the future of Deposit Claims within a broader function responsible for end-to-end claims processing across all dispute types. With accountability for approximately 1,000 employees across the U.S., India, and the Philippines, the role combines significant operational scale with responsibility for strengthening claims operations, risk and control outcomes, and the customer experience. As a key leader within Fraud Operations, this individual will influence enterprise priorities and partner across the organization to strengthen the performance and long-term direction of Deposit Claims.

Make a lasting impact by protecting customers, developing high-performing leaders, and advancing a resilient Deposit Claims organization that delivers strong risk, service, and operational outcomes.

In this role, you will:
- Lead a large, specialized organization of managers and individual contributors responsible for executing risk-based fraud and claims programs
- Establish and strengthen risk policies, procedures, and controls that support Deposit Claims and broader enterprise priorities
- Monitor fraud and claims activity, emerging risks, and performance trends to anticipate issues and guide timely action
- Set strategic priorities and make decisions that strengthen claims performance, risk management, operational efficiency, and customer outcomes
- Partner with Fraud Operations leaders and enterprise stakeholders to align priorities, influence decisions, and deliver coordinated outcomes
- Direct the allocation of people and financial resources to meet operational commitments and advance business priorities
- Build leadership capability and a strong talent pipeline that supports team member growth, engagement, and organizational performance

Required Qualifications:
- 10+ years of Fraud Claim Investigation or Policy Violations, Risk Management, or Compliance experience, including Management or leadership experience, or equivalent experience demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education
- 4+ years of management or leadership experience
- Extensive experience leading fraud and claims operations within large, complex organizations, with deep expertise in Deposit Claims operations and inherent risk
- Demonstrated success leading diverse, geographically dispersed operations teams, managing people and financial resources, and fostering a culture of service, accountability, engagement, and efficiency

Desired Qualifications:
- Experience leveraging digital contact center technologies, automation, and process modernization to improve customer and operational outcomes
- Deep understanding of the regulatory and control environment governing consumer deposit claims, including dispute resolution and customer remediation
- Strong analytical judgment with the ability to translate operational and risk data into actionable insights
- Experience developing operational strategies, governance, and performance measures that balance customer, risk, efficiency, and business outcomes
- Proven ability to navigate complexity, lead change, and drive sustained execution across a large operation
- Demonstrated ability to influence and align senior leaders across Operations, Risk, Compliance, Technology, Product, and Legal to deliver enterprise-wide outcomes
- Track record of developing senior leaders and building succession pipelines for complex operations organizations

jobs.description:
Why Wells Fargo

Are you looking for more? Find it here. At Wells Fargo, we're more than a financial services leader –we’re a global trailblazer committed to driving innovation, empowering communities, and helping our customers succeed. We believe that a meaningful career is much more than just a job – it’s about finding all of the elements to help you thrive, in one place.

Living the Well Life means you’re supported in life, not just work. It means having robust benefits, competitive compensation, and programs designed to help you find work-life balance and well-being.

You’ll be rewarded for investing in your community, celebrated for being your authentic self, and empowered to grow. Join us!

About this role

Wells Fargo is seeking a Principal Architect within the Chief Operating Office Technology portfolio to define and execute the architecture strategy for Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB) post-trade functions. This leader will align technology investments with business growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, resilience, and modernization priorities.

As the portfolio’s senior architecture authority, you will partner with business and technology leaders to establish target-state architectures across applications, data, integrations, cloud platforms, and emerging technologies, delivering scalable, secure solutions for CIB post-trade operations.

The role requires deep financial services, enterprise architecture, and modern engineering expertise to lead technology transformation, simplify complex ecosystems, establish reusable data and integration standards, and advance cloud-native, AI-enabled, and automated capabilities. In addition, you will help shape future-state architecture strategies across the broader Consumer & Investment Banking technology organization.

In this role, you will:

- Apply deep Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB) post-trade expertise, enterprise architecture leadership, data and integration strategy, and modern AI and engineering capabilities to lead hands-on solution architecture and execution.

- Act as a trusted advisor to business and technology leadership to develop or influence architecture solutions supporting investment advisory, brokerage, wealth management, portfolio management, trading, and client servicing platforms.

- Lead architecture strategy and resolution of highly complex technology challenges across corporate and investment banking products and services.

- Provide vision, direction, and expertise to senior leadership on implementing the transformation strategy describing the current state, target state, and transition architecture

- Provide vision, direction, and expertise for innovative technology solutions that improve investor experience and advisor effectiveness.

- Design and drive implementation of AI-driven solutions to support advisor workflows, investment research, client communications, compliance monitoring, and operational efficiency.

- Partner with risk, compliance, legal, and regulatory teams to ensure architectures support SEC, FINRA, and other applicable regulatory requirements.

- Promote architecture standards aligned with enterprise banking and investment technology strategies.

- Maintain awareness of emerging technologies, digital assets and AI capabilities that create competitive advantages in investment services.

- Engage strategically with senior leaders across technology, product, operations, risk, compliance, and investment businesses.

jobs.title: Associate, Investment Banking - Fund Solutions
jobs.description:
Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB) delivers a comprehensive suite of banking, capital markets and advisory solutions, including a full complement of sales, trading and research capabilities, to corporate, government and institutional clients. We focus on our clients' overall financial needs, with consideration and respect for their total relationship with Wells Fargo.

About this role:

The Fund Finance team provides fund-level financing through structured credit facilities and capital market solutions to private capital funds and other asset managers. Fund Finance is part of the Corporate and Investment Bank (CIB). Team members support our focus on building strong customer relationships balanced with a strong risk mitigation and compliance-driven culture that firmly establishes those disciplines as critical to the success of our customers and company.

As part of the broader Fund Finance team, the Fund Solutions team focuses on providing asset managers and private capital investors differentiated Fund Finance products spanning across Net Asset Value (NAV) financing, Structured Products (Collateralized Fund Obligations/Rated Feeders), Advisory Services and Capital Raising Solutions. The Fund Solutions product set spans across a wide array of financing and capital raising solutions which may be suitable for the bank’s balance sheet and/or distribution to the growing non-bank lender universe (e.g., Insurance Companies and Private Credit Investors).

Fund Solutions is looking for an Associate to support the origination, structuring and execution of Fund Solutions products, with a particular focus on structured products such as Collateralized Fund Obligations (CFOs) and rated feeder solutions. The ideal candidate will bring strong technical and transaction execution capabilities, including financial modeling, portfolio analysis, transaction structuring, coordination of rating agency and investor workstreams, legal documentation, and execution through closing. Given the breadth of the Fund Solutions product set, the team is seeking a dynamic candidate who can think independently, manage complex workstreams and help build a fast-growing business within Fund Finance.

In this role, you will:

Structuring and Transaction Execution:

- Manage transaction execution from initial deal preparation and structuring through marketing, investor diligence, documentation, and closing;
- Build and maintain detailed transaction models for CFOs, rated feeders, Secondary NAV facilities, and other structured or lending transactions;
- Analyze portfolio characteristics including projected cash flows, investment strategies, and fund seasoning to develop suitable financing solutions and portfolio construction;
- Conduct thorough due diligence including reviewing financial statements, fund documents and legal agreements;
- Work closely with rating agencies to obtain debt ratings.

Other General Responsibilities:

- Prepare client presentations, transaction materials, term sheets, internal approval memoranda, and investor marketing materials;
- Perform credit underwriting for new transactions and support annual reviews of existing facilities;
- Prepare borrowing base calculations in Excel;
- Work closely with internal and external counsel to negotiate legal documentation;
- Negotiate, structure, and execute amendments and other facility modifications;
- Partner with analysts and internal partners to manage internal compliance, booking, and funding processes.
- Contribute to portfolio analysis across the broader Fund Finance team portfolio.

Required Qualifications:

- 2+ years of Investment Banking experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education

Desired Qualifications:

- Experience with originating and monitoring subscription facilities, NAV facilities, asset backed finance facilities, securitizations, or other structured products is strongly preferred.
- Highly knowledgeable of private capital, fund finance, and structured finance industries including structure (e.g. waterfall, amortization profile, etc.), investment strategies, cash flows, performance metrics, and various product use cases.
- Ability to analyze large data sets to provide insights on expected fund performance, pricing strategies, and optimal structuring.
- Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail and accuracy.
- Very comfortable and efficient in Excel. Experience writing formulas; organizing, analyzing, and formatting data; and recognizing and auditing errors.
- Ability to manage a high-volume workload while maintaining excellence and consistency of work.  Ability to quickly change focus and stay organized is a must.
- Ability to work effectively, as well as independently, in a team environment.
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
- Experience reading, negotiating, and/or interpreting legal documents.
- High level of personal motivation. Does more than what is asked for and anticipates questions/issues.
- Direct client interaction experience, including some experience interacting with senior decision makers.
- Willingness to work 50+ hours per week, depending on workload.

Job Expectations:

- Obtaining and/or maintaining appropriate Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) license(s) is required for ongoing employment in this position. FINRA Series 63 and 79 examinations, or equivalent must be completed within either a 90 or 180-day time period following commencement of employment, depending upon the number of license(s) needed if not immediately available to transfer upon hire. FINRA recognized equivalents will be accepted. This will be communicated at time of offer acceptance. Compliance with state law registration and licensing requirements is mandatory. In addition to state registration and licensing requirements, specific product licenses or SAFE licensing may apply. Additional requirements include meeting enhanced financial fitness and criminal background standards. Wells Fargo will initiate the FINRA licensing review process at the time of offer acceptance. For specific FINRA qualification exams obtained after 9/30/2018, the Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) exam co-requisite is required.
- This position is subject to FINRA background screening requirements. Candidates must successfully complete and pass a background check prior to hire. In accordance with FINRA rules, individuals who are subject to statutory disqualification are not eligible to be associated with a FINRA-registered broker-dealer. Successful candidates must also meet and comply with ongoing regulatory obligations, which include periodic screening and mandatory reporting of certain incidents.
- Specific compliance policies may apply regarding outside activities or personal investing; affected employees will be expected to provide information to the Wells Fargo Personal Account Dealing Team and abide by applicable policy requirements if hired. Information will be shared about expectations during the recruitment process.
- Ability to travel up to 10% of the time
